exceptions.reason: Accepted documented risk for SUPPLY-86eeb375, re-verified 2026-08-01 (Foundation-Loop E-7cd17680). GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 affects only unstable React Server Component APIs. probectl ships a client-only BrowserRouter with basename /ui, and the named guard rejects RSC APIs, RSC build dependencies, RSC entrypoints, server-action directives, and any loss of that exact browser-router seam. As of 2026-08-01 the only patched release is react-router 8.3.0 — a major outside the installed 7.x line; the newest 7.x (7.18.2) remains inside the official affected range >=7.12.0 <8.3.0, so no compatible patched release exists. Renewed to 2026-10-31; revisit on a 7.x backport, the React Router 8 upgrade decision, or advisory change, whichever comes first. A new advisory, affected-range drift, installed-version change, RSC/server-action adoption, audit clearance, or expiry fails closed and reopens review.

Accepted documented risk for SUPPLY-1dbf9837. GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff is a Windows-only alternate-path bypass in Vite server.fs.deny. probectl pins Vite 5.4.21 only as local dev/build tooling; Vite is absent from the shipped browser bundle and Go binaries, and the production-only npm audit is unaffected. Decision of record 2026-08-01 (Foundation-Loop E-00330a5d): upgrade to the current Vite 8 line (8.2.0 at decision time) and land it before this exception's 2026-09-30 boundary with the web build, bundle-budget, rendered-a11y, and coverage gates green; the minimal patched hop to 6.4.3 is rejected because it lands two majors behind and pays the migration cost twice. The boundary is therefore a landing deadline, not a rolling renewal — if the upgrade has not landed by expiry the gate goes red by design. A new advisory, affected-range drift, installed-version change (including the planned Vite bump), production reachability, audit clearance, or expiry fails closed and reopens review.

Accepted documented risk for SUPPLY-f205d4eb if the exact historical transitive node reappears: brace-expansion 1.1.16 was reachable only through local dev/build glob tooling, never shipped in the browser runtime, and received no untrusted product input; no patched 1.x exists. The current lock uses patched 5.0.8, so this standing exception is dormant and accepts nothing today. A new advisory, advisory-range drift, any installed-version change, production reachability, or expiry fails closed.
